verses.text: After this I looked and saw a door standing open in heaven. And the voice I had previously heard speak to me like a trumpet was saying, "Come up here, and I will show you what must happen after these things."
At once I was in the Spirit, and I saw a throne standing in heaven, with someone seated on it.
The One seated there looked like jasper and carnelian, and a rainbow that gleamed like an emerald encircled the throne.
Surrounding the throne were twenty-four other thrones, and on these thrones sat twenty-four elders dressed in white, with golden crowns on their heads.
From the throne came flashes of lightning, and rumblings, and peals of thunder. Before the throne burned seven torches of fire. These are the seven Spirits of God.
And before the throne was something like a sea of glass, as clear as crystal. In the center, around the throne, were four living creatures, covered with eyes in front and back.
The first living creature was like a lion, the second like a calf, the third had a face like a man, and the fourth was like an eagle in flight.

And each of the four living creatures had six wings and was covered with eyes all around and within. Day and night they never stop saying: "Holy, Holy, Holy, is the Lord God Almighty, who was and is and is to come!"
And whenever the living creatures give glory, honor, and thanks to the One seated on the throne who lives forever and ever,
the twenty-four elders fall down before the One seated on the throne, and they worship Him who lives forever and ever. They cast their crowns before the throne, saying:
"Worthy are You, our Lord and God, to receive glory and honor and power, for You created all things; by Your will they exist and came to be."

context.author: John, who was on the island of Patmos (1:1, 4, 9); traditionally the apostle John
context.genre: Apocalypse, prophecy, and letter, full of symbols and visions
context.audience: Seven churches in the Roman province of Asia
context.setting: John looks and sees an open door in heaven. A voice invites him up, and he sees a throne with one seated on it, surrounded by twenty-four elders on thrones, a sea of glass, and four living creatures who never cease to say, “Holy, Holy, Holy” The elders cast their crowns before the throne.
context.custom: Roman emperors were worshiped as lords and gods, with titles such as “Lord and God.” Here the elders cast their crowns before the one true Lord, a claim that in John’s day challenged the empire. The rainbow around the throne recalls God’s covenant after the flood.
context.timelineImmediate: Chapter 5 shows a sealed scroll and the Lamb who is worthy to open it.
context.timelineBible: The throne room draws on Isaiah 6, Ezekiel 1 and 10, and Daniel 7. The four living creatures combine features of Ezekiel’s cherubim and Isaiah’s seraphim.

translation.meaning: Deserving, fitting. Used of those entitled to honor.
The seat of rule, used more than 40 times in Revelation.

otBackground.note: The Lord seated on a throne, “Holy, holy, holy.”
The four creatures and the throne.

overview.summary: John sees the throne of God in heaven, surrounded by elders and living creatures in ceaseless worship of the Creator.

history.t: Asian cities had temples to the emperor.
Jewish visions of God’s court were common.

archaeology.t: A temple honoring the emperor in John’s city.
Winged creatures in Assyrian and Babylonian art.

archaeology.h: Early Christian Art of the Throne
archaeology.t: The apse mosaic of Santa Pudenziana in Rome, about AD 400, shows Christ enthroned with the four living creatures in the sky, one of the earliest pictures of this chapter.

overview.discussion: In heaven the worship is centered on who God is. How does my own worship compare, and where does my attention drift?
overview.book: The book of Revelation · 22 chapters. A vision of Christ, judgment, and the new creation, written to encourage persecuted believers.
overview.author: John

timeline.label: The open door and the throne

historicalImage.caption: The apse mosaic of Santa Pudenziana in Rome, of about AD 400, one of the oldest in the city. Christ is enthroned among the apostles before a heavenly city, with the four living creatures of Revelation 4 in the sky above.

currentImage.caption: The fortified Monastery of St John the Theologian on the hilltop of Patmos, founded by the monk Christodoulos in 1088. John says he was on Patmos “because of the word of God and my testimony about Jesus” (Revelation 1:9).
